stories.headline: RBA lifts cash rate to 15-year high of 4.6 per cent
stories.facts: The Reserve Bank of Australia increased the cash rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.6 per cent, reaching a 15-year high. Australia's annual headline inflation rate rose to 4 per cent for the 12 months to August 2026, driven by a 14.8 per cent spike in fuel prices. Economists note that larger average home loans and higher household debt levels compared to 2011 mean rate rises have a more severe impact on mortgage holders.
key_numbers: Cash rate: 4.6 per cent following a 0.25 percentage point increase
Annual headline inflation: 4 per cent for the 12 months to August 2026
Average mortgage variable rate: between 6.24 and 6.62 per cent for owner-occupiers
Average first-home buyer loan size: $731,000 in 2026
stories.why_it_matters: Higher interest rates increase monthly repayments for mortgage holders, with average owner-occupiers spending between $4,500 and $4,680 per month, while continuing rate pressures may also affect rental costs and small business margins.

debate.question: Are mortgage holders bearing an unfair share of the burden in the fight against inflation?

sides.position: Borrowers are being punished twice through high prices and high interest rates, while essential expenses cannot easily be reduced.
sides.evidence: Average mortgages have more than doubled since 2011 alongside higher living costs and increased loan sizes.

sides.position: Higher interest rates are necessary to curb excess demand and reduce the far worse long-term consequences of persistent inflation.
sides.evidence: Annual headline inflation rose to 4 per cent in August 2026, demonstrating that inflation remains above target.

stories.headline: Major banks pass RBA rate rise in full as cash rate hits 4.60%
stories.facts: The Reserve Bank of Australia lifted the official cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.60%. Commonwealth Bank, Westpac, National Australia Bank and ANZ announced they will pass the full 0.25 percentage point increase onto variable home loan customers from 9 October. Commonwealth Bank also confirmed eligible variable-rate business loans will rise by 0.25 percentage points from the same date.
key_numbers: Cash rate: 4.60%, up 25 basis points
Headline inflation: 4.0% in the year to August, up from 3.5% in July
Westpac's lowest variable rate: rises from 5.99% to 6.24% on 9 October
Trimmed mean inflation: 3.6% for August
stories.why_it_matters: Mortgage holders will face higher monthly repayments starting in October, with business borrowers also experiencing increased financing costs as lenders pass on the RBA rate hike.

debate.question: Will the Reserve Bank of Australia raise the cash rate again in November 2026?

sides.evidence: Cite rising energy prices linked to the Middle East conflict and persistent inflationary pressures.

sides.position: Expect rates to hold in November
sides.evidence: Point to the RBA's stated strategy of preserving labour market gains and an incremental approach to policy adjustment.

stories.headline: Specialist crews remove 31-tonne whale carcass from City Beach
stories.facts: Specialist contractors using heavy machinery, an excavator and a truck began removing a 13-metre, 31-tonne humpback whale carcass from South City Beach on Wednesday. The Town of Cambridge estimated the removal and landfill disposal costs at between $60,000 and $100,000. The presence of the carcass drew large crowds and attracted several great white sharks close to shore, prompting a beach closure, exclusion zones and $250 fines for unauthorized access.
key_numbers: Whale weight: 31 tonnes
Whale length: 13 metres
Removal cost estimate: $60,000 to $100,000
Council fine for breaching exclusion zone: $250
stories.why_it_matters: City Beach remains closed to swimmers and visitors while heavy machinery operations and shark monitoring continue due to public safety risks.

stories.headline: Kondinin Wind Farm Reaches Financial Close for 130MW Stage 1
stories.facts: Foresight Group reached financial close on the 130MW first stage of the Kondinin Wind Farm in Western Australia's Wheatbelt, securing A$430 million in debt financing to begin construction. Foresight acquired full ownership of the broader 370MW project after buying out Shell Energy's 50% stake. Stage 1 will use 21 Vestas turbines, is backed by a 7-year Power Purchase Agreement with Synergy and a 15-year Australian Government Capacity Investment Scheme agreement, and is designated as a Priority Project under the State Development Act.
key_numbers: Debt financing secured: A$430 million
Capacity: 130MW for Stage 1 (370MW total project)
Turbines: 21 Vestas V162-6.2 MW turbines
Direct construction jobs: 145 jobs
stories.why_it_matters: Construction will commence with completion expected to supply renewable electricity to the South West Interconnected System from late 2028, generating enough energy to power up to 70,000 homes while supporting regional jobs.

stories.headline: Great white sharks circle Swanbourne beach after whale carcass washes ashore
stories.facts: Surf Life Saving WA reported a whale carcass washed ashore near Swanbourne in Perth on Monday morning. The Surf Life Saving helicopter spotted three four-metre great white sharks circling about 15 metres from the shore at approximately 2.45pm, alongside a hammerhead and two tiger sharks in nearby waters. City Beach was closed one kilometre north and south of the location as a precaution while authorities manage the carcass.
key_numbers: Shark sightings: Three four-metre great white sharks circling 15 metres from shore
Beach closure zone: One kilometre north and south of City Beach
stories.why_it_matters: Beachgoers and swimmers face heightened shark risks along Perth's coastline due to the whale carcass acting as an attractant, prompting municipal beach closures.

stories.headline: Whale Carcass at City Beach Prompts Closures and Shark Sightings
stories.facts: A whale carcass washed up at City Beach on Monday, drawing several sharks including two great whites measuring 5 metres and 4 metres just 10 metres from the shore. The Town of Cambridge closed local beaches for three days and prepared for a removal operation estimated to cost between 40,000 and 60,000 Australian dollars. Fisheries Minister Jackie Jarvis stated that towing the carcass out to sea was avoided due to the risk of it breaking up and washing back ashore.
key_numbers: Shark sizes: 5 metres and 4 metres for the two observed great whites
Removal cost estimate: 40,000 to 60,000 Australian dollars
Historical removal cost: 175,000 Australian dollars for a whale at Scarborough Beach in 2014
stories.why_it_matters: Beachgoers face ongoing closures across the Town of Cambridge until the carcass is removed and water conditions are declared safe, while local authorities manage the removal costs.

stories.headline: WA Government considers Bullsbrook quarantine centre for prison use
stories.facts: Western Australia's Corrective Services Commissioner Brad Royce and Corrective Services Minister Tony Buti stated on Wednesday that the $400 million Commonwealth-owned Bullsbrook quarantine centre remains under consideration for conversion into a prison if it becomes available. A feasibility study began in June, driven by overcrowding and a prison population strain that led to a "show cause" notice for Hakea, Casuarina and Melaleuca prisons. Simultaneously, the state announced a $100 million court security arrangement employing 127 full-time staff under the Sheriff's Office to free up 45,000 police hours.
key_numbers: Facility value: $400 million
Bed expansion: 480 beds at Acacia Prison by 2029
Court security funding: $100 million
New court security staff: 127 full-time staff
stories.why_it_matters: The proposal to convert the quarantine facility faces local opposition, including a parliamentary petition with 165 signatures from residents, while the broader prison system deals with overcrowding and triple-bunking.

debate.question: Should the Commonwealth-owned Bullsbrook quarantine centre be converted into a prison to address Western Australia's prison overcrowding?

sides.position: The state government is keeping the option open and conducting feasibility assessments to secure additional space amid severe prison population pressures.
sides.evidence: Corrective Services Commissioner Brad Royce stated he is looking for space and would be interested if the site becomes available, while Minister Tony Buti said nothing is off the cards.

sides.position: The government should not retrofit a facility never built to be a prison and should instead invest in properly planned, long-term infrastructure, with local residents opposing the site's proximity.
sides.evidence: Shadow corrective services minister Adam Hort argued the plan stems from a failure to plan ahead and wastes money that could fund long-term expansion, alongside a parliamentary petition of 165 local signatures opposing the move.

stories.headline: JCDecaux Launches Nurture for Country Campaign with Chalkwest
stories.facts: JCDecaux launched its Nurture for Country program with its first partner, Chalkwest, an Aboriginal-owned vehicle rental provider in Western Australia. The campaign aims to elevate First Nations businesses through Out-of-Home advertising, starting with a phase delivered in collaboration with Perth Airport before rolling out across the state. Chalkwest is led by Managing Director Zak Kirkup and operates a fleet of more than 1,300 vehicles across 12 towns and seven airports.
key_numbers: Fleet size: More than 1,300 vehicles across Chalkwest's network
Operating footprint: 12 towns and 7 airports throughout Western Australia
Airport passenger reach: More than 18 million passengers pass through Perth Airport annually
stories.why_it_matters: Chalkwest gains increased visibility across JCDecaux's digital and transit advertising network to support business growth and community initiatives, reaching millions of passengers at Perth Airport.

stories.headline: Australia bans card payment surcharges starting October
stories.facts: New payment scheme rules following an RBA review take effect to end payment surcharges for EFTPOS, Visa, Mastercard, American Express, UnionPay, and PayPal. Payment networks have integrated bans into merchant contracts, and terminal software will be updated automatically to disable surcharge features. Standard weekend hospitality surcharges, public holiday fees, and ticketing booking fees remain legal if applied independently of payment method, while RBA consumer credit card interchange fee caps drop from 0.80 per cent to 0.30 per cent.
key_numbers: 16 per cent of Australian businesses historically surcharged
0.80 per cent to 0.30 per cent cap reduction on consumer credit cards
stories.why_it_matters: Consumers will pay the advertised sticker price without checkout surcharges, while merchants face restructured processing fees that may influence retail pricing.

stories.headline: August inflation jumps to 4 per cent as rate hike fears grow
stories.facts: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reported headline inflation jumped to 4.0 per cent in the year to August, up from 3.5 per cent in July. Automotive fuel prices surged 15 per cent following Middle East conflict and the end of fuel excise relief, while new dwelling prices rose 5.4 per cent over 12 months. Underlying trimmed mean inflation remained steady at 3.6 per cent.
key_numbers: 4.0 per cent annual headline inflation
3.5 per cent previous inflation rate
15 per cent fuel price surge
3.6 per cent underlying inflation
stories.why_it_matters: Higher inflation figures increase the probability of the Reserve Bank of Australia raising interest rates further before the end of the year.

stories.headline: Reserve Bank of Australia raises cash rate to 4.60 per cent
stories.facts: The Reserve Bank of Australia's Monetary Policy Board voted unanimously to raise the official cash rate target by 25 basis points to 4.60 per cent, taking effect on September 30, 2026. The RBA cited headline inflation climbing to 4.0 per cent in August and persistent capacity constraints as drivers for the fourth rate hike of the year. Underlying trimmed mean inflation remained at 3.6 per cent, and the unemployment rate stood at 4.6 per cent.
key_numbers: 4.60 per cent cash rate
25 basis points increase
4.0 per cent August headline inflation
4.6 per cent unemployment rate
stories.why_it_matters: Mortgage holders face immediate increases in minimum monthly repayments as borrowing costs reach a 15-year high.

stories.headline: WA Government provides up to $4 million to restart Cardup brickworks
stories.facts: The Western Australian Government is providing up to $4 million to support the recommissioning of the mothballed Austral brickworks in Cardup. The facility is expected to produce approximately 17 million Maxibricks and increase state brick production by 10 to 15 per cent once operational. The funding package includes a $3 million upfront contribution for maintenance, a $500,000 incentive to resume operations by March 2027, and a $500,000 incentive for delivering 17 million bricks within 12 months.
key_numbers: Funding amount: up to $4 million provided by the State Government
Production increase: 10 to 15 per cent boost to Western Australia's brick supply
Output target: 17 million Maxibricks
Housing commencements: over 24,200 homes since April 2023
stories.why_it_matters: The restart of the Cardup facility aims to ease building material shortages and support residential construction activity across Western Australia.

stories.headline: News Australia and CommBank launch national housing affordability campaign
stories.facts: News Australia and CommBank launched a national campaign named 'The Home Front' on Monday across news.com.au and State & Community mastheads. The campaign is informed by the National Housing Affordability Project research conducted in July by The Growth Distillery and SEC Newgate Research surveying 2,048 Australians aged 18 and over. The survey found that 53 per cent of non-homeowners want to buy a first home but only 14 per cent believe it will happen soon, 51 per cent of aspiring first-home buyers have surrendered hope, and 68 per cent of renters believe they will rent for life.
key_numbers: Survey sample size: 2,048 Australians aged 18+
Non-homeowners wanting to buy: 53%
Non-homeowners expecting to buy soon: 14%
Aspiring first-home buyers who gave up hope: 51%
stories.why_it_matters: The multi-platform campaign examines economic pressures like negative gearing, capital gains tax, interest rates, stamp duty and land tax, while exploring alternative solutions such as modular housing and downsizing.

stories.headline: Greens leader Larissa Waters steps down due to health reasons
stories.facts: Australian Greens Leader Larissa Waters announced she is stepping down from the party leadership due to a downturn in her pre-existing kidney disease. Senator Waters said the demands of leadership and travel are incompatible with her recovery, though her prognosis is positive. She will remain in parliament as a Senator for Queensland and take a period of medical leave. A party room meeting will be held later this week to elect a new leader.
key_numbers: 19 months: length of time Senator Waters served as party leader
2010: year Senator Waters was first elected as Senator for Queensland
stories.why_it_matters: The resignation triggers a leadership race within the Greens party ahead of the next federal election, with a new leader to be selected by the party room later this week.

stories.headline: Australian household spending unchanged in August as transport offsets falls
stories.facts: Australian household spending was unchanged in seasonally adjusted terms in August, following increases of 1.1 per cent in July and 0.9 per cent in June, according to Australian Bureau of Statistics data. ABS head of business statistics Tom Lay reported that recreation and culture spending saw the largest fall at 1.4 per cent, alongside declines in clothing and footwear, recreational goods, food, health, and furniture. These falls were offset by a 2.3 per cent increase in transport spending driven by an 8.1 per cent rise in fuel spending following the full restoration of fuel excise duty on August 3.
key_numbers: 1.4 per cent: fall in recreation and culture spending in August
2.3 per cent: rise in transport spending in August
8.1 per cent: rise in fuel spending in August
stories.why_it_matters: The stagnation in household spending indicates a cooling in consumer demand across most retail sectors, with higher fuel costs shifting household expenditure towards transport.

stories.headline: Victorian doctors stage mass walkout over pay and working conditions
stories.facts: Thousands of doctors from major Victorian hospitals will walk off the job on Thursday afternoon for a four-hour strike. The action follows over 14 months of negotiations with the Victorian government. Doctors are calling for a 30 per cent pay rise over four years, a 12.5-hour shift cap, paid overtime, and three consecutive days off per fortnight.
key_numbers: Shift length cap demanded: 12.5 hours
Pay rise demanded: 30% over four years
Negotiation duration: More than 14 months across more than 60 meetings
stories.why_it_matters: Patients face delayed non-critical and elective surgeries across Victorian hospitals as doctors strike over fatigue and safety concerns.

stories.headline: Terra Metals Confirms High-Grade Reef Discovery in Southwest
stories.facts: Terra Metals announced the discovery of what it describes as the Southwest’s largest continuous high-grade reef at its Western Australia project. Following the confirmation, company shares fell by 3%. Detailed figures and operational data were not available in the provided text.
key_numbers: Share price change: Down 3% following the announcement
stories.why_it_matters: Investors face a minor drop in share value following the announcement, while the company advances its exploration project in Western Australia.

stories.headline: RBA says home price plunge poses no major stability risk
stories.facts: The Reserve Bank of Australia stated in its half-yearly Financial Stability Review that less than one per cent of borrowers are estimated to be facing negative equity. RBA modelling suggests that housing prices could fall by 20 per cent from current levels and only about five per cent of mortgages would enter negative equity. The report follows the RBA lifting interest rates by 25 basis points to 4.6 per cent on Tuesday, while headline inflation rose to 4.0 per cent.
key_numbers: 1 per cent: estimated borrowers facing negative equity
20 per cent: potential housing price fall examined in RBA modelling
25 basis points: interest rate hike on Tuesday
4.6 per cent: new interest rate level
stories.why_it_matters: Mortgage holders face higher borrowing costs following the RBA's fourth rate rise of 2026, but the central bank assesses that household and business financial sectors remain resilient overall with low arrears rates.

stories.headline: Ampol buys Evie Networks for $225 million
stories.facts: Fuel giant Ampol agreed to acquire 100 per cent of Evie Networks for $225 million, adding more than 1,000 charging bays to its existing network. The combined platform will feature 1,425 charging bays across more than 400 sites, with the transaction expected to complete in the first half of 2027 subject to ACCC clearance. Ampol reported that charging sessions and energy volume on its AmpCharge network more than doubled in the first half of 2026.
key_numbers: $225 million purchase price
1,000 charging bays added
1,425 combined charging bays
400 sites
stories.why_it_matters: The acquisition expands Ampol's public electric vehicle charging infrastructure as national electric vehicle sales rise to represent over 25 per cent of new car sales.

stories.headline: National dwelling approvals drop 6.1 per cent in August
stories.facts: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reported that total dwelling approvals fell 6.1 per cent in August to 16,953. Private sector house approvals rose 3.7 per cent to 10,885 dwellings, marking eight consecutive months above 10,000. Private sector dwellings excluding houses fell 21.2 per cent to 5,674 dwellings, driven by declines in apartment and townhouse approvals.
key_numbers: 16,953 total dwellings approved in August
6.1 per cent fall in total dwellings
10,885 private sector houses approved
21.2 per cent fall in non-house dwellings
stories.why_it_matters: The decline in apartment and non-house approvals threatens the federal government's target of building 1.2 million new homes by June 2029.

stories.headline: Australian Consumer Price Index Rises 4.0 Percent in Year to August 2026
stories.facts: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reported that the Consumer Price Index rose 4.0 per cent in the 12 months to August 2026, up from 3.5 per cent in July. Housing was the largest contributor to annual inflation, increasing by 5.7 per cent due to higher costs for new dwellings and electricity. Transport was the second largest contributor, rising by 5.6 per cent driven by automotive fuel prices, which jumped 14.8 per cent in August.
key_numbers: Consumer Price Index annual rise: 4.0% in the 12 months to August 2026
Housing annual inflation: 5.7% in August 2026
Transport annual inflation: 5.6% in August 2026
Trimmed mean annual inflation: 3.6% in August 2026
stories.why_it_matters: Higher inflation erodes household purchasing power across Australia and maintains pressure on the Reserve Bank regarding interest rates.

stories.headline: Australian Greens elect David Shoebridge as new leader
stories.facts: The Australian Greens party room elected David Shoebridge as its new leader in an 11-member ballot in Sydney, following the resignation of Larissa Waters due to ill health. Senator Shoebridge defeated Mehreen Faruqi seven votes to four after preferences, with Steph Hodgins-May elected as deputy leader. Senator Shoebridge stated that the party aims to replace the Labor Party and focus on the cost of living and corporate opposition.
key_numbers: Leadership ballot: 7 votes to 4 won by David Shoebridge over Mehreen Faruqi
Deputy leadership ballot: 6 votes to 5 won by Steph Hodgins-May over Vanessa Bleyer
stories.why_it_matters: Changes in leadership shift the parliamentary strategy and policy focus of the federal Greens party as they position themselves against both major parties.

stories.headline: Australian House Prices and Debt Surge Compared to Past High Interest Rates
stories.facts: The Reserve Bank increased the cash rate to 4.6 per cent, marking a level not seen since October 2011 when the rate sat at 4.75 per cent. Cotality data shows that median house values have more than doubled since 2011 while wages have increased by about 49 per cent. The national dwelling value to income ratio has risen from 6.5 times to 8.7 times, and household debt has grown from 161 per cent to 178 per cent of disposable incomes.
key_numbers: Cash rate: 4.6%
Sydney median house value in October 2011: $598,888
Melbourne median house value in October 2011: $472,705
Perth median house value in October 2011: $460,361
stories.why_it_matters: Higher mortgage repayments and elevated debt levels relative to incomes increase financial stress for Australian households as they service larger mortgages under higher interest rates.

stories.headline: David Shoebridge Elected Leader of the Australian Greens
stories.facts: Senator David Shoebridge won a contested vote to become the new leader of the Australian Greens, running on a ticket with deputy Stephanie Hodgins-May. Shoebridge defeated senators Sarah Hanson-Young and Mehreen Faruqi for the position. In his first speech, Shoebridge stated his goal to build a mass movement to replace the federal Labor Party and criticised the government over economic inequality.
key_numbers: Age of David Shoebridge: 55
Age of Stephanie Hodgins-May: 41
Greens vote share between recent elections: 12%
Shoebridge political career duration: 16 years
stories.why_it_matters: The leadership change affects how the Greens negotiate key legislation with the federal government and shapes the minor party's political strategy heading toward future elections.

stories.headline: WA Government invests over $2 million in Mid West racing infrastructure
stories.facts: The Western Australian Government is investing more than $2 million into Geraldton Turf Club and Dongara Irwin Race Club. Geraldton Turf Club completed a $1.163 million irrigation system project and received $40,000 for rubber flooring in horse stalls, with further upgrades underway. Dongara Irwin Race Club is utilizing a $92,000 funding package for water system improvements and horse stall roofing.
key_numbers: Total government investment: More than $2 million
Geraldton Turf Club irrigation project: $1.163 million
Dongara Irwin Race Club package: $92,000
Regional racing economic contribution: $37.6 million annually to the State economy
stories.why_it_matters: Regional racing clubs in Western Australia receive upgraded infrastructure to support animal welfare, safety, and continued economic contributions to the state.

stories.headline: Mining couple stages gender reveal using Kalgoorlie Super Pit blast
stories.facts: Kalgoorlie Super Pit workers Lance and Kristy Richards used the mine's daily explosives blast mixed with pink powder for a gender reveal. The couple conceived after an 11-year IVF journey and are expecting a baby girl in January. Northern Star Resources human resources manager Nicole Musgrave approved the special request.
key_numbers: IVF journey duration: 11 years
Super Pit workforce: 1,800 total employees, approximately 35% female
Mine dimensions: 4km long and 1.6km at widest point
stories.why_it_matters: The event highlights employee milestones at one of Australia's largest gold mines and brings public attention to the challenges of the IVF process.

stories.headline: Former Obstetrician Restores Western Australian Wheatbelt Property to Bushland
stories.facts: Dr Susan Downes, a 76-year-old former GP obstetrician, has spent 11 years restoring a 200-hectare rural property north of York in Western Australia's wheatbelt. Aided by volunteers, she has planted approximately 45,000 trees across five planting seasons with a survival rate exceeding 40%. The property includes Mount Mackie, a site historically significant from Ensign Robert Dale's 1830 expedition and valued by local Indigenous communities.
key_numbers: Property size: 200 hectares
Trees planted: Approximately 45,000 over five planting seasons
Tree survival rate: More than 40 per cent
Volunteer list: About 80 individuals on the Friends of Mount Mackie list
stories.why_it_matters: The revegetation project converts degraded agricultural land back into native York gum and wandoo bushland, providing a conservation model in a region where over 90 per cent of the wheatbelt has been cleared.

stories.headline: WA opposition criticises government over use of school transportable classrooms
stories.facts: The WA opposition accused the state government of poor planning after a new parliamentary document revealed that over 4,000 transportable classrooms are currently in use across Western Australian schools, representing nearly one in six classrooms. Opposition education spokesman Liam Staltari stated that newer schools opened since 2017 are heavily reliant on demountables, with more than half of all classrooms at Wellard Primary School, Oakwood Primary School and Aspiri Primary School being transportable. Education Minister Sabine Winton defended the use of transportables as a cost-effective way to rapidly increase capacity, and stated that 11 new primary schools and two new high schools will be built between now and 2030 to address demand and remove transportables.
key_numbers: 4,000 transportables: placed across WA schools
30 new primary schools and 8 secondary schools: opened since 2017
240 students: capacity of a new permanent addition funded for Riva Primary School
stories.why_it_matters: Schools relying on transportable classrooms face constrained green space and ovals, while students and teachers use temporary buildings. Planned construction projects and budget allocations aim to deliver permanent facilities in fast-growing suburbs by 2030.

stories.headline: Analysis Shows Australian Politicians Lead in AI Speech Usage
stories.facts: An analysis by The Economist found that Australian politicians lead the English-speaking world in using artificial intelligence to write or assist with speeches. A random sample of parliamentary speeches between September 2025 and 2026 showed that more than 20 per cent of House of Representatives speeches and just under 15 per cent of Senate speeches were flagged by the Pangram AI content detector. Speaker Milton Dick stated there are no parliamentary rules governing the use of AI in speeches, though members remain responsible for their statements.
key_numbers: House of Representatives AI-flagged speeches: more than 20%
Senate AI-flagged speeches: just under 15%
Senior staffer base salary for speechwriters: $140,000
stories.why_it_matters: The high volume of AI-assisted political speech has sparked debate among MPs, speechwriters, and independent figures regarding transparency, constituent trust, and the loss of authentic human perspective in parliament.

stories.headline: Special WA Police powers take effect for Land Forces conference
stories.facts: The Cook Labor Government's Land Forces (Special Powers) Act 2026 is in full effect from 1 to 10 October 2026. The legislation gives WA Police additional powers within designated security areas around the Perth Convention and Exhibition Centre, where the Land Forces 2026 event runs from 6 to 8 October. Police Minister Reece Whitby stated the powers include establishing checkpoints, cordons, and roadblocks, searching people, bags, and vehicles, and issuing lawful directions, last used during the 2011 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting.
key_numbers: 10 October 2026: Expiry date for special police powers
6-8 October: Dates for the Land Forces 2026 event
10 days: Duration of the temporary police powers
stories.why_it_matters: Attendees, workers, and the wider community in Perth are affected by increased police presence, checkpoints, and potential delays around the Perth Convention and Exhibition Centre during the event period.

stories.headline: Western Australia government provides $4 million bailout to restart Cardup brickworks
stories.facts: The Western Australia government announced a support package of up to $4 million on September 29 to recommission the mothballed Austral brickworks at Cardup in south-eastern Perth. The package includes a $3 million upfront payment, a $500,000 incentive payment to resume production by March 2027, and $500,000 to deliver 17 million maxibricks within 12 months of opening. Housing Industry Association WA executive director Michael McGowan stated the support will boost state brick production by 10 to 15 per cent and support a broad cross-section of construction projects.
key_numbers: $4 million government assistance package
10 to 15 per cent increase in state brick production
17 million maxibricks to be delivered within 12 months
24,200 homes in housing starts since April 2023
stories.why_it_matters: The funding aims to ease supply rationing by the state's main brick producer and support the construction of schools, hospitals, commercial developments and residential housing across Western Australia.

stories.headline: Mosman Park woman charged with attempted murder of husband
stories.facts: Gay Bernadette Branchi, 88, was arrested and charged with attempted murder over allegations she tried to kill her husband, former Automotive Holdings Group chairman Robert Branchi. The accused was taken into custody from The Queenslea residential aged care home in Claremont where the couple shared a room. Following an initial court appearance via audio link and magistrate concerns regarding cognitive mental capacity and vulnerability, Mrs Branchi was granted bail.
key_numbers: Aged care deposit: reportedly exceeding $1.6 million at The Queenslea
Mosman Park home purchase price: $1.5 million in 1995
Shareholding history: more than 17 million shares held by Robert Branchi in 2007
stories.why_it_matters: The legal proceedings progress through the courts following a bail review for the elderly resident of a Claremont aged care facility.

stories.headline: Man arrested after shots fired and pedestrian targeted in Rokeby
stories.facts: Tasmania Police took a man into custody and set up crime scenes at Burtonia Street in Rokeby and Holmfield Avenue in Clarendon Vale following a reported shooting on Wednesday at around 11:30am. Police stated a vehicle pulled up beside a walking pedestrian, and a single shot was fired in their direction before the vehicle left. No injuries were reported, the firearm and suspect vehicle were located, and Bellerive officers, the Special Operations Group and South East CIB are involved in the investigation.
key_numbers: Incident time: 11:30am Wednesday
stories.why_it_matters: Residents in Rokeby and Clarendon Vale experienced police cordons and an armed response following the incident, with authorities seeking dashcam and CCTV footage.

stories.headline: Dead humpback whale removed from Perth's City Beach
stories.facts: A 72-tonne crane hired by the Town of Cambridge began lifting a 13-metre long, decomposing humpback whale carcass at about 10am at Perth's City Beach. The whale washed up on Monday and initially weighed 31 tonnes before being wrapped in a net and dragged 1.5 kilometres along the shore. Town of Cambridge Mayor Gary Mack stated the plan was to bury the whale in landfill and that the council planned to pay for the removal, while not ruling out asking the state government to foot the bill.
key_numbers: 72-tonne crane used for the lift
13-metre long decomposing carcass
1.5 kilometres distance dragged along the shore
$100,000 operation cost
stories.why_it_matters: The removal operation cost $100,000 and required local road and beach management, while the presence of the carcass drew large crowds and tagged white sharks to the area.

stories.headline: Edith Cowan University joins Additive Manufacturing Cooperative Research Centre
stories.facts: Edith Cowan University (ECU) has joined the Additive Manufacturing Cooperative Research Centre (AMCRC) as its newest research partner. The addition expands the AMCRC's research network to 12 universities and CSIRO. ECU will contribute to collaborative research programs, project development and workforce initiatives focused on additive manufacturing.
key_numbers: 12 universities and CSIRO in the network
stories.why_it_matters: The partnership connects ECU directly with manufacturers to develop and commercialise solutions intended to improve productivity and support Western Australia's resources, defence and mining sectors.

stories.headline: US Court of International Trade hears challenge to Donald Trump's latest tariffs
stories.facts: The US Court of International Trade heard arguments on Wednesday in a legal challenge brought by importers and 25 Democrat-led states against the Trump administration's 10 to 12.5 per cent tariffs imposed in late July on about 60 economies and 86 countries. The tariffs were implemented under Section 301 of the US Trade Act on the grounds that foreign failures to prevent imports of goods made with forced labour burdened US commerce. The challengers argued the tariffs are a pretext to recreate a global tariff regime previously ruled illegal by the courts and that the administration failed to follow required country-specific investigative processes.
key_numbers: 10 to 12.5 per cent: tariff rates imposed on about 60 economies and 86 countries
12.5 per cent: tariff rate applied to Australian exports to the US

stories.headline: Sydney Metro to keep six platform doors closed on final M1 line section
stories.facts: Sydney Metro has assured safety regulators it will keep six train and platform screen doors closed at stations along the final section of the $30 billion M1 metro line. Three screen doors will remain closed at Dulwich Hill station, and one each at Canterbury, Campsie and Marrickville, located at curved platforms where the distance between trains and platforms is widest. Transport Minister John Graham stated that 170 mechanical gap fillers have been installed across eight stations to ensure safe boarding.
key_numbers: $30 billion cost of M1 metro line
6 screen doors to remain closed
170 mechanical gap fillers installed
8 stations affected by curved platforms
stories.why_it_matters: Commuters awaiting the opening of the final 13-kilometre section between Sydenham and Bankstown face continued delays while the national rail regulator completes its safety review.

stories.headline: ABS Grants Approval in Principle to Hanwha Ocean Floating Data Center
stories.facts: ABS has issued approval in principle to Hanwha Ocean for the concept design of a 60 megawatt floating data center. The concept design combines shipbuilding and offshore engineering expertise to address land, power, and cooling constraints of conventional facilities. The approval remains at the concept stage, with no construction order, deployment location, or project timeline disclosed.
key_numbers: Capacity: 60 megawatts for the Hanwha Ocean floating data center concept
Capacity range: 50 to 200 megawatts for conceptual floating data centers approved by ABS over the past year
stories.why_it_matters: Developers can use the certified offshore design as a baseline to address power and cooling bottlenecks associated with land-based digital infrastructure.
